# Expert Dental Month 1 — retrospective and future Sprint canon

## 0. Authority boundary

This document records lessons from Expert Dental/Raimov for **future CAESTHETIC scoping and add-on decisions**. It does not add, remove, merge, reinterpret or retroactively reprice any of the 16 items in `docs/ssot/EXPERT_DENTAL_MONTH_1_PLAN_AND_REPORTS.md`. It does not change current Expert Dental obligations, statuses, evidence or results. The historical plan and its period files remain authoritative for that client period.

Reusable CAESTHETIC product and recurring-scope authority remains `docs/ssot/CAESTHETIC.md`; operating automation and request routing remain in `docs/ssot/CAESTHETIC_GROWTH_SYSTEM_OPERATING_MODEL.md`.

Cross-repo note: these CAESTHETIC authorities live in `zaomir/grainee-v2`. The `zaomir/raimovdental` satellite mirrors this Expert Dental retrospective and Raimov operating docs, but it does not become a second authority for the CAESTHETIC master/economics/operating-model files.

## 1. Retrospective conclusion

The Expert Dental first-month plan combined diagnosis, deep research, multi-surface implementation, content production, reputation maintenance, team behavior change and standalone internal systems. Taken together, that is too broad for a repeatable standard 30-day Sprint. The lesson is about future scope design, not a judgment that the historical plan should be rewritten.

Future Sprints should concentrate execution on the few binding constraints that can be shipped and evidenced in 30 days. Recurring processes and standalone systems must be identified at intake instead of being absorbed as unlimited Sprint work.

## 2. Lean future Sprint template

Select approximately **3–6 Category A main constraints** to complete or materially resolve and **1–5 Category B processes** that are genuinely launched but require an objective observation horizon. These ranges are planning limits, not output quotas.

A reasonable Month-1 shape is:

1. measurement foundation and source discipline;
2. the patient conversion path from inquiry to booking/consultation;
3. maps/entity cleanup;
4. one production-ready compliant reputation loop;
5. one or two high-ticket offer paths; and
6. an administrator conversion kit with scripts, SLA and follow-up rules.

Do not include by default: deep research across 10–15 competitors; a full blog plus mass article production; recurring maps/review maintenance; full-team training/change management; custom internal software unless a Build-vs-Configure Gate proves the need; routine social management; or paid-media management.

Every future Sprint must include:

- **Day-0 Access Gate** — accounts, permissions, owners and approvals are explicit;
- **Before Snapshot** — dated baseline evidence for selected constraints;
- **One Revenue Recovery Loop where applicable** — reactivation, abandoned lead, no-show or unclosed-consultation recovery;
- **Live Evidence per task** — a live artifact/system state, not a draft or activity claim;
- **Client Growth Statement** — the short owner-facing result layer alongside the detailed evidence layer; and
- **Build-vs-Configure Gate** — configure/reuse first; custom build only when justified and correctly scoped.

## 3. What may mature into Month 2 or recurring ownership

Review velocity, map movement, content expansion, reactivation cycles, attribution/CRM data discipline, administrator adoption and internal referrals may move into Month 2 or Growth System only when the process was truly launched in Month 1 and needs time or recurring ownership to produce observable evidence. This is maturation, not an artificial backlog.

A Sprint Extension is justified only for finite implementation blocked by access, client approval, vendor dependency or an objective implementation horizon. Work that was reasonably completable in Month 1 may not be held back to create a second Sprint.

## 4. Standalone modules and add-on boundary

The following are independently valuable systems and are not free expansions of a Sprint or the client-specific Growth System Fixed Management Fee:

- Recruitment Hub or another recruitment/staffing system;
- a complex Review Hub beyond a proportionate reputation optimization;
- patient motivation, membership or loyalty systems;
- a custom internal workspace, portal or operations application; and
- comparable multi-role systems with their own build, rollout, QA and change-management load.

Use the four-class Client Request Router in `docs/ssot/CAESTHETIC_GROWTH_SYSTEM_OPERATING_MODEL.md`:

- `Included Optimization` for proportionate changes to an existing approved growth path;
- `Growth Budget Cost` for approved client-funded inputs;
- `Growth Add-on` for bounded new growth assets/systems; and
- `Practice Operations Add-on` for staffing and operations systems that directly support patient acquisition, conversion, retention or service operations.

Recruitment/staffing systems, concierge operations, internal training infrastructure and workflow/QA design normally route to **Practice Operations Add-on**. Ongoing ownership is a separate monthly add-on; finite implementation is fixed-price. A useful request is offered a route rather than refused automatically, but it is not silently included because it is urgent or adjacent to marketing.

## 5. Administrator operating model

Use **solid line to clinic / dotted operational line to CAESTHETIC Patient Operations**.

The clinic remains the employer and retains payroll, hiring/firing, HR, scheduling, disciplinary and clinical authority. CAESTHETIC may own the agreed operational layer: response SLA, CRM discipline, scripts, follow-up, lost-lead recovery, VIP journey, service QA, training and performance metrics. CAESTHETIC may recommend staffing changes but does not become the employer or clinical manager by implication.

Recommended compensation principle:

`base salary + Patient Operations Bonus + VIP Concierge Bonus`

Bonuses should use service/operational KPI such as response discipline, CRM completeness, follow-up completion, show-up support, handoff quality, VIP-service completion and QA—not a percentage of medical treatment value. A treatment-value percentage is not the default and must not be canonized as one.

If a percentage is required, it may apply only to a separately priced **non-clinical concierge/service fee**, and only after local employment, healthcare, tax and accounting review. Every jurisdiction requires local employment/healthcare review before launch; the clinic keeps final HR and clinical authority.

## 6. Positioning lesson

CAESTHETIC is not evolving into a less-defined, broader agency. It is an external **Growth + Patient Operations desk**. Recruitment and adjacent functions are allowed as paid add-ons only when they directly support patient acquisition, conversion, retention or patient-service operations and pass the appropriate legal, employer, privacy and clinical boundaries.

## 7. Reporting lesson

Expert Dental keeps its detailed plan/status/material/evidence system. The owner-facing layer is shorter, mobile-first and result-oriented. It answers what became better in the business during the period, separates activity from verified result and uses `Shipped → Adopted → Impact → Maturing`. The detailed dual-axis rules are in `docs/raimov/operations/expert-dental/PLANNING_AND_REPORTING.md`; reusable statement and evidence controls are in `docs/ssot/CAESTHETIC_GROWTH_SYSTEM_OPERATING_MODEL.md`.
